similarities.claim: Supports custom modes that tailor behavior and permissions for different tasks.

differences.claim: Roo Code is editor-centric, while AFOL is a project-local kernel and scaffold.

lessons_for_afol.lesson: Mode and rule surfaces should be explicit, inspectable, and bounded by task intent.
Permission boundaries should be represented as data rather than hidden prompt behavior.

do_not_copy.reason: Do not couple AFOL governance to one editor UI or assume interactive approvals are always available.

source_refs.title: Roo Code custom modes
source_refs.claim: Roo Code documents custom modes that can specialize behavior and restrict access to files, commands, or tools.
